text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: real-time latency regression detected for prod /api/v1/generate. p95=480ms (alert 400ms), p99=1.2s (alert 1.0s). paging @oncall :pager:

emma: saw the page, on it. quick sanity checks: is this region-specific?

raj: Grafana quick view shows spike starting ~2590001180, mostly in us-west1. link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/prod?panelId=23&orgId=1

emma: thanks. can someone check recent deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy completed: service=runtime-api image=model-server:v2.5 commit=ab12cd 2590001200 by ci/cd

oliver: 2 things to check: 1) model variant v2.5 introduced a kv-cache change, 2) we had a small autoscaler hiccup at ~2590001160.

courtney: loading some logs now. streaming tails show stalls: repeated "write timeout to client" and intermittent "kv-cache-miss backlog" in runtime logs. snippet:

```
[2590001223] WARN runtime: kv-cache miss backlog=142 ms=0.002
[2590001231] ERROR stream: stall detected id=session-xxxx elapsed=540ms
[2590001240] WARN svc: request queued > 120ms
```

marta: checking customer impact dashboards — sessions with streaming enabled show p99 jump from 350ms -> 1.1s, error-rate increase to 0.9% (baseline 0.1%). a handful of enterprise customers have elevated tail latency; support is getting tickets.

emma: ok, mitigation options: rollback v2.5, route traffic to dedicated pool, or enable fallback to v2.4 model-variant. rollback might be disruptive if in-flight streams. prefer traffic routing / fallback for quick mitigation.

raj: agree. quick test: route 10% traffic to v2.4 and observe. I can flip the routing in control plane.

emma: do it. set a canary and monitor p95/p99 metrics and streaming error rates.

raj: running control-plane API now:
```
POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/routesets/production/overrides
{
  "rule":"fallback-quick-dial",
  "conditions": {"model":"model-x","variant":"v2.4"},
  "traffic_pct": 10
}
```

deploy-bot: route update accepted. change_id=chg-7591

oliver: initial feedback: 10% on v2.4 p95=210ms p99=520ms for those sessions. overall prod p95 drops to 390ms in 2m.

emma: good sign. escalate to 30% gradually to avoid cache cold start. raj, please ramp to 30% over 5min.

raj: ramping now + monitor.

[~2m later]

raj: at 30% now. prod p95=360ms p99=680ms. streaming error-rate down to 0.4%. artifacts still present in some pods.

courtney: investigating node-level metrics: a subset of pods on host-gpu-12 show high kernel stalls and GPU mem pressure coincident with kv-cache shrink. likely a kernel-level scheduling issue + cache policy change in v2.5.

marta: support report: customer "BrightLeaf" reported degraded streaming for ~10m, escalated to SEs. communication: we should send incident ack and ETA for mitigation.

emma: i'll post status update to #support and external status page: "Investigating latency regression affecting streaming p99, mitigation in progress via traffic routing and fallback. No data exfiltration. Next update in 15m."

emma: also paging infra-sre @oliver for possible node remediation (drain/restart) if routing doesn't stabilize.

oliver: on it. prepping a graceful drain on gpu-12 nodes after we finish ramp. will coordinate to avoid breaking existing streams (drain schedule: 1 node at a time, cordon -> drain -> restart -> uncordon).

raj: current thought: keep 30% on v2.4 for 15m observing, if p99 < 800ms and error-rate < 0.5% then roll permanent routing until we can fix v2.5 cache behavior.

emma: agreed. also create a metric alert for "kv-cache-miss-backlog > 100" to catch recurrence.

courtney: added temporary alert rule: kv-cache-backlog-high_persist 5m -> paging.

marta: filed incident in airflow: INC-259-2026; tagged impacted customers + SE contacts.

emma: timeline so far: 2590001180 spike start, deploy v2.5 @2590001200, p95/p99 rising by 2590001220, first page 2590001234. mitigation routing to v2.4 begun 2590001250.

oliver: quick check on hotfix feasibility: we could revert the kv-cache patch in v2.5 and do a hot-redeploy to a subset, but that takes ~20-30m validation. prefer routing until we have a safe patch.

raj: monitoring sliding window. adding a short-lived dashboard panel for v2.4 vs v2.5 latency split: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/split/variant-latency?orgId=1

[~10m later]

raj: observed stabilization: global p95=330ms, p99=620ms. streaming error-rate 0.25%.

marta: customers notified. no new major customer tickets.

emma: good. action items: 1) keep 30% on v2.4 and schedule rollback or targeted revert in v2.5 tomorrow; 2) follow-up postmortem; 3) add runtime guard to prevent kv-cache shrink in the hot path without canary; 4) update runbook with model-variant fallback steps.

courtney: logging follow-up: collect full stack traces and kernel logs from affected hosts and attach to incident. I'll start an automated gather job.

oliver: proceeding with one-node drain trial on host-gpu-12 in 10m; will report.

emma: handing off active on-call to courtney for next 2 hours while I jump to customer sync. courtney, you have ownership: please keep ramp commit in control plane and update here.

courtney: taking over. confirmed 30% persistent. will update every 15min or on changes.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: NOTE: paging shift recorded. current incident state: mitigation-in-progress. incident id=2590001234.

emma: thanks team. post-incident: schedule a deep dive with runtime and infra next week to nail root cause and timeline for fix.

courtney: logging final note for now: observed contributing factors: model-variant change (v2.5), kv-cache behavior, autoscaler noise — combined led to tail build-ups. Next update in 15m or earlier. :thumbsup:
